text: THE aphorism, "As a man thinketh in his heart so is he," not only embraces the whole of a man's being, but is so comprehensive as to reach out to every condition and circumstance of his life. A man is literally _what he thinks,_ his character being the complete sum of all his thoughts.
note: How habitual thoughts shape who you become

tags.when_helps: Someone wondering how much their thoughts shape who they are and how their life goes.

display_text: THE aphorism, "As a man thinketh in his heart so is he," not only embraces the whole of a man's being, but is so comprehensive as to reach out to every condition and circumstance of his life. A man is literally what he thinks, his character being the complete sum of all his thoughts.
plain: The saying "as a man thinks in his heart, so is he" covers a person's whole being and every circumstance of life: you literally are what you think, your character being the total of all your thoughts.
core_idea: You are what you think

text: MAN'S mind may be likened to a garden, which may be intelligently cultivated or allowed to run wild; but whether cultivated or neglected, it must, and will, _bring forth._ If no useful seeds are _put_ into it, then an abundance of useless weed-seeds will _fall_ therein, and will continue to produce their kind. Just as a gardener cultivates his plot, keeping it free from weeds, and growing the flowers and fruits which he requires, so may a man tend the garden of his mind, weeding out all the wrong, useless, and impure thoughts, and cultivating toward perfection the flowers and fruits of right, useful, and pure thoughts. By pursuing this process, a man sooner or later discovers that he is the master-gardener of his soul, the director of his life.
note: Negative thought spirals; tending your mind

tags.when_helps: Someone whose mind feels overrun by unhelpful thoughts, wanting to tend it deliberately.

plain: The mind is like a garden that grows something whether tended or not; neglected, it fills with weeds. Weed out wrong, impure thoughts and grow right, pure ones, and you find you are the master gardener of your soul.
core_idea: Tend your mind like a garden

text: As a progressive and evolving being, man is where he is that he may learn that he may grow; and as he learns the spiritual lesson which any circumstance contains for him, it passes away and gives place to other circumstances.
note: Stuck in a hard situation; learning from it

tags.when_helps: Someone stuck in a hard circumstance who wants to believe it has something to teach and will pass.

display_text: As a progressive and evolving being, man is where he is that he may learn that he may grow; and as he learns the spiritual lesson which any circumstance contains for him, it passes away and gives place to other circumstances.
plain: As a growing being, a person is where he is in order to learn and grow; once he learns the spiritual lesson a circumstance holds for him, it passes and gives way to other circumstances.
core_idea: Circumstances pass once we learn their lesson

text: Man is buffeted by circumstances so long as he believes himself to be the creature of outside conditions, but when he realizes that he is a creative power, and that he may command the hidden soil and seeds of his being out of which circumstances grow, he then becomes the rightful master of himself.
note: Feeling powerless against circumstances

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling buffeted by circumstances and powerless to change them.

display_text: Man is buffeted by circumstances so long as he believes himself to be the creature of outside conditions, but when he realizes that he is a creative power, and that he may command the hidden soil and seeds of his being out of which circumstances grow, he then becomes the rightful master of himself.
plain: A person is tossed about by circumstances as long as he believes he is their creature; once he realises he is a creative power who can direct the hidden seeds circumstances grow from, he becomes master of himself.
core_idea: Knowing you can shape circumstances makes you their master

text: Men are anxious to improve their circumstances, but are unwilling to improve themselves; they therefore remain bound. The man who does not shrink from self-crucifixion can never fail to accomplish the object upon which his heart is set. This is as true of earthly as of heavenly things. Even the man whose sole object is to acquire wealth must be prepared to make great personal sacrifices before he can accomplish his object; and how much more so he who would realize a strong and well-poised life?
note: Wanting change without changing yourself

tags.when_helps: Someone who wants better circumstances but has not yet faced what they must change in themselves.

display_text: Men are anxious to improve their circumstances, but are unwilling to improve themselves; they therefore remain bound. The man who does not shrink from self-crucifixion can never fail to accomplish the object upon which his heart is set. This is as true of earthly as of heavenly things. Even the man whose sole object is to acquire wealth must be prepared to make great personal sacrifices before he can accomplish his object; and how much more so he who would realize a strong and well-poised life?
plain: People want better circumstances but won't improve themselves, so they stay stuck. Whoever doesn't shrink from sacrificing himself will reach what his heart is set on; even getting rich demands sacrifice, so how much more a strong, balanced life?
core_idea: To change circumstances, first be willing to change yourself

text: Good thoughts and actions can never produce bad results; bad thoughts and actions can never produce good results. This is but saying that nothing can come from corn but corn, nothing from nettles but nettles. Men understand this law in the natural world, and work with it; but few understand it in the mental and moral world (though its operation there is just as simple and undeviating), and they, therefore, do not co-operate with it.
note: Choices and consequences; reaping what you sow

tags.when_helps: Someone wondering why their life keeps producing the same results, open to looking at their thinking.

display_text: Good thoughts and actions can never produce bad results; bad thoughts and actions can never produce good results. plain: Good thoughts and acts never bring bad results, nor bad ones good: corn yields only corn, nettles only nettles. People follow this law in nature, but few see it works just as surely in the mind and morals.
core_idea: Good thoughts bear good fruit, bad thoughts bad

text: A man only begins to be a man when he ceases to whine and revile, and commences to search for the hidden justice which regulates his life. And as he adapts his mind to that regulating factor, he ceases to accuse others as the cause of his condition, and builds himself up in strong and noble thoughts; ceases to kick against circumstances, but begins to _use_ them as aids to his more rapid progress, and as a means of discovering the hidden powers and possibilities within himself.
note: Blaming others; turning hardship into growth

tags.when_helps: Someone blaming others for their situation who is ready to be challenged to use it instead.

display_text: A man only begins to be a man when he ceases to whine and revile, and commences to search for the hidden justice which regulates his life. And as he adapts his mind to that regulating factor, he ceases to accuse others as the cause of his condition, and builds himself up in strong and noble thoughts; ceases to kick against circumstances, but begins to use them as aids to his more rapid progress, and as a means of discovering the hidden powers and possibilities within himself.
plain: You begin to be a real man when you stop whining and cursing and look for the hidden justice ruling your life; then you stop blaming others, think nobly, and use circumstances to grow and find your hidden powers.
core_idea: Stop blaming; use circumstances to grow

text: A particular train of thought persisted in, be it good or bad, cannot fail to produce its results on the character and circumstances. A man cannot _directly_ choose his circumstances, but he can choose his thoughts, and so indirectly, yet surely, shape his circumstances.
note: Feeling powerless over circumstances

tags.when_helps: Someone who cannot change their circumstances directly and wants to know what they can change.

display_text: A particular train of thought persisted in, be it good or bad, cannot fail to produce its results on the character and circumstances. A man cannot directly choose his circumstances, but he can choose his thoughts, and so indirectly, yet surely, shape his circumstances.
plain: Any line of thought kept up, good or bad, will shape character and circumstances. You can't directly choose your circumstances, but you can choose your thoughts, and so shape your circumstances indirectly but surely.
core_idea: Choose your thoughts and you shape your circumstances

text: Let a man cease from his sinful thoughts, and all the world will soften towards him, and be ready to help him; let him put away his weakly and sickly thoughts, and lo, opportunities will spring up on every hand to aid his strong resolves; let him encourage good thoughts, and no hard fate shall bind him down to wretchedness and shame. The world is your kaleidoscope, and the varying combinations of colours, which at every succeeding moment it presents to you are the exquisitely adjusted pictures of your ever-moving thoughts.
note: Outlook shaping how the world feels

tags.when_helps: Someone stuck in weak or gloomy thinking who wants to believe changing it could open new doors.

display_text: Let a man cease from his sinful thoughts, and all the world will soften towards him, and be ready to help him; let him put away his weakly and sickly thoughts, and lo, opportunities will spring up on every hand to aid his strong resolves; let him encourage good thoughts, and no hard fate shall bind him down to wretchedness and shame. The world is your kaleidoscope, and the varying combinations of colours, which at every succeeding moment it presents to you are the exquisitely adjusted pictures of your ever-moving thoughts.
plain: Give up sinful thoughts and the world softens toward you; drop weak thoughts and opportunities appear; nurture good thoughts and no hard fate can keep you miserable. The world is a kaleidoscope mirroring your changing thoughts.
core_idea: The world mirrors your thoughts

text: If you would protect your body, guard your mind. If you would renew your body, beautify your mind. Thoughts of malice, envy, disappointment, despondency, rob the body of its health and grace. A sour face does not come by chance; it is made by sour thoughts. Wrinkles that mar are drawn by folly, passion, and pride.
note: Bitterness and envy wearing a person down

tags.when_helps: Someone noticing how malice, envy or despondency are wearing on their body and face.

display_text: If you would protect your body, guard your mind. If you would renew your body, beautify your mind. Thoughts of malice, envy, disappointment, despondency, rob the body of its health and grace. A sour face does not come by chance; it is made by sour thoughts. Wrinkles that mar are drawn by folly, passion, and pride.
plain: To protect your body, guard your mind; to renew it, beautify your mind. Malice, envy, disappointment and gloom rob the body of health and grace; sour thoughts make a sour face, and folly, passion and pride make wrinkles.
core_idea: Guard your mind to protect your body

text: There is no physician like cheerful thought for dissipating the ills of the body; there is no comforter to compare with goodwill for dispersing the shadows of grief and sorrow. To live continually in thoughts of ill will, cynicism, suspicion, and envy, is to be confined in a self made prison-hole. But to think well of all, to be cheerful with all, to patiently learn to find the good in all--such unselfish thoughts are the very portals of heaven; and to dwell day by day in thoughts of peace toward every creature will bring abounding peace to their possessor.
note: Cynicism and resentment as a self-made prison

tags.when_helps: Someone sunk in cynicism, suspicion or sorrow who wants a way out through goodwill toward others.

text: A man should conceive of a legitimate purpose in his heart, and set out to accomplish it. He should make this purpose the centralizing point of his thoughts. It may take the form of a spiritual ideal, or it may be a worldly object, according to his nature at the time being; but whichever it is, he should steadily focus his thought-forces upon the object, which he has set before him. He should make this purpose his supreme duty, and should devote himself to its attainment, not allowing his thoughts to wander away into ephemeral fancies, longings, and imaginings. This is the royal road to self-control and true concentration of thought. Even if he fails again and again to accomplish his purpose (as he necessarily must until weakness is overcome), the _strength of character gained_ will be the measure of _his true_ success, and this will form a new starting-point for future power and triumph.
note: Aimlessness; finding purpose; failing repeatedly

tags.when_helps: Someone drifting without direction, or failing repeatedly at a goal and needing to keep at it.

core_idea: Fix your thoughts on one purpose; failures build strength

text: The weakest soul, knowing its own weakness, and believing this truth _that strength can only be developed by effort and practice,_ will, thus believing, at once begin to exert itself, and, adding effort to effort, patience to patience, and strength to strength, will never cease to develop, and will at last grow divinely strong.
note: Feeling weak; building strength through effort

tags.when_helps: Someone who feels weak and doubts they can grow stronger.

display_text: The weakest soul, knowing its own weakness, and believing this truth that strength can only be developed by effort and practice, will, thus believing, at once begin to exert itself, and, adding effort to effort, patience to patience, and strength to strength, will never cease to develop, and will at last grow divinely strong.
plain: Even the weakest soul, knowing its weakness and believing strength comes only through effort and practice, will start trying, and by adding effort to effort and patience to patience will keep growing until it becomes divinely strong.
core_idea: Strength grows through steady effort and patience

text: The will to do springs from the knowledge that we _can_ do. Doubt and fear are the great enemies of knowledge, and he who encourages them, who does not slay them, thwarts himself at every step.
note: Self-doubt and fear holding you back

tags.when_helps: Someone held back by doubt and fear before something they want to do.

display_text: The will to do springs from the knowledge that we can do. Doubt and fear are the great enemies of knowledge, and he who encourages them, who does not slay them, thwarts himself at every step.
plain: The will to act comes from knowing we can. Doubt and fear are the great enemies of that knowledge, and whoever feeds them instead of killing them blocks himself at every step.
core_idea: Doubt and fear block the will to act

text: A strong man cannot help a weaker unless that weaker is _willing_ to be helped, and even then the weak man must become strong of himself; he must, by his own efforts, develop the strength which he admires in another. None but himself can alter his condition.
note: Trying to help someone who must help themselves

tags.when_helps: Someone hoping another will rescue them, or trying to help someone not yet willing to change.

display_text: A strong man cannot help a weaker unless that weaker is willing to be helped, and even then the weak man must become strong of himself; he must, by his own efforts, develop the strength which he admires in another. None but himself can alter his condition.
plain: A strong person can't help a weaker one unless the weaker is willing, and even then the weak must grow strong by his own effort; no one but himself can change his condition.
core_idea: No one but yourself can change your condition

text: He who would accomplish little must sacrifice little; he who would achieve much must sacrifice much; he who would attain highly must sacrifice greatly.
note: Ambition and the cost of achievement

tags.when_helps: Someone with a big ambition weighing what it will cost them.

display_text: He who would accomplish little must sacrifice little; he who would achieve much must sacrifice much; he who would attain highly must sacrifice greatly.
plain: Small achievements need small sacrifices; great achievements need great ones; the highest attainments need the greatest sacrifice.
core_idea: Achievement is measured by sacrifice

text: The greatest achievement was at first and for a time a dream. The oak sleeps in the acorn; the bird waits in the egg; and in the highest vision of the soul a waking angel stirs. Dreams are the seedlings of realities.
note: Holding on to a dream that seems distant

situations: loss of a dream or plan
a career change or new job
tags.when_helps: Someone holding a dream that still feels far off and needing encouragement to keep it.

display_text: The greatest achievement was at first and for a time a dream. The oak sleeps in the acorn; the bird waits in the egg; and in the highest vision of the soul a waking angel stirs. Dreams are the seedlings of realities.
plain: Every great achievement began as a dream. The oak sleeps in the acorn, the bird waits in the egg, and in the soul's highest vision an angel is stirring. Dreams are the seedlings of reality.
core_idea: Dreams are the seeds of reality

text: The thoughtless, the ignorant, and the indolent, seeing only the apparent effects of things and not the things themselves, talk of luck, of fortune, and chance. Seeing a man grow rich, they say, "How lucky he is!" Observing another become intellectual, they exclaim, "How highly favoured he is!" And noting the saintly character and wide influence of another, they remark, "How chance aids him at every turn!" They do not see the trials and failures and struggles which these men have voluntarily encountered in order to gain their experience; have no knowledge of the sacrifices they have made, of the undaunted efforts they have put forth, of the faith they have exercised, that they might overcome the apparently insurmountable, and realize the Vision of their heart. They do not know the darkness and the heartaches; they only see the light and joy, and call it "luck". They do not see the long and arduous journey, but only behold the pleasant goal, and call it "good fortune," do not understand the process, but only perceive the result, and call it chance.
note: Envying others' success as mere luck

tags.when_helps: Someone envying others' success as luck, or whose own hidden struggle goes unseen.

core_idea: What people call luck is unseen effort

text: In all human affairs there are _efforts,_ and there are _results,_ and the strength of the effort is the measure of the result. Chance is not. Gifts, powers, material, intellectual, and spiritual possessions are the fruits of effort; they are thoughts completed, objects accomplished, visions realized.
note: Effort versus waiting for luck

tags.when_helps: Someone wanting results without effort, or doubting that their effort will count.

display_text: In all human affairs there are efforts, and there are results, and the strength of the effort is the measure of the result. Chance is not. Gifts, powers, material, intellectual, and spiritual possessions are the fruits of effort; they are thoughts completed, objects accomplished, visions realized.
plain: In everything there is effort and result, and the result matches the strength of the effort; there is no chance. Gifts and possessions of every kind are the fruit of effort: thoughts completed, goals reached, visions made real.
core_idea: Results match effort; there is no chance

text: CALMNESS of mind is one of the beautiful jewels of wisdom. It is the result of long and patient effort in self-control. Its presence is an indication of ripened experience, and of a more than ordinary knowledge of the laws and operations of thought. A man becomes calm in the measure that he understands himself as a thought evolved being, for such knowledge necessitates the understanding of others as the result of thought, and as he develops a right understanding, and sees more and more clearly the internal relations of things by the action of cause and effect he ceases to fuss and fume and worry and grieve, and remains poised, steadfast, serene.
note: Worry and agitation; cultivating calm

tags.when_helps: Someone given to worry and fuss who wants to grow steady and serene over time.

display_text: CALMNESS of mind is one of the beautiful jewels of wisdom. It is the result of long and patient effort in self-control. plain: Calmness is a jewel of wisdom, earned by long patient self-control. As you understand yourself and others as shaped by thought, and see cause and effect more clearly, you stop fussing, worrying and grieving, and stay steady and serene.
core_idea: Understanding cause and effect brings calm

text: Tempest-tossed souls, wherever ye may be, under whatsoever conditions ye may live, know this in the ocean of life the isles of Blessedness are smiling, and the sunny shore of your ideal awaits your coming. Keep your hand firmly upon the helm of thought. In the bark of your soul reclines the commanding Master; He does but sleep: wake Him. Self-control is strength; Right Thought is mastery; Calmness is power. Say unto your heart, "Peace, be still!"
note: Feeling overwhelmed and storm-tossed

tags.when_helps: Someone tossed about by turmoil who needs a call to steady their mind and find calm.
